claims.text: The untreated metallic or alloy components are susceptible to wear under aggressive environmental conditions.
The untreated metallic or alloy components are susceptible to corrosion under aggressive environmental conditions.
The untreated metallic or alloy components are susceptible to fatigue under aggressive environmental conditions.
A nanostructured ceramic coating can be deposited by plasma spraying or sol–gel processing.
Applying a nanostructured ceramic coating will improve the surface physical and mechanical characteristics of the components.
The coating's refined grain-boundary architecture and enhanced densification will impede crack propagation.
The coating's refined grain-boundary architecture and enhanced densification will impede diffusion of corrosive species.
The coating will reduce surface roughness and surface defects.
The coating will provide a chemically inert barrier that reduces corrosion.
The coating will provide a mechanically robust barrier that reduces wear.
Nanostructured grains will improve load distribution at the coating–substrate interface.
Nanostructured grains will mitigate mechanical deformation under cyclic stress.
Coated components will have a lower wear rate than uncoated components.
Coated components will have greater resistance to pitting and corrosion than uncoated components.
Coated components will have a longer fatigue life than uncoated components.
The improvements will remain effective under cyclic thermal loading, high humidity, acidic or saline atmospheres, and mechanical abrasion.
Non-optimized coating thickness can diminish the coating's benefits.
Compromised substrate–coating adhesion can diminish the coating's benefits.
Exceeding the coating design's thermal or mechanical limits can diminish its benefits.
No eligible cited record directly supports this coating approach under the stated conditions.
